sources.entry: YouTube Music - Desktop player for YouTube Music with plugin support. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/th-ch/youtube-music/) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Pear Desktop (formerly th-ch/youtube-music) is an unofficial, volunteer-built desktop wrapper for YouTube Music with a native look and a plugin system.
summary.what_it_does: Pear Desktop wraps the YouTube Music web service in a desktop application with a native look and feel. The README says it is an independent, non-profit, unofficial project not affiliated with Google or YouTube. Users can load CSS files to restyle the app through Options > Visual Tweaks > Themes. A plugin API lets developers hook into the Electron BrowserWindow in the main process, inject CSS, change the HTML in the renderer, and communicate between front and back via IPC. The README also covers installation through several package managers and a development workflow using pnpm, with optional devcontainers, and builds for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
use_cases: listen to YouTube Music in a standalone desktop window
restyle YouTube Music with custom CSS themes
add custom features to YouTube Music via plugins
install a desktop music player on macOS, Windows, or Linux
build a YouTube Music desktop client from source
write an Electron plugin that changes the player UI
how_to_run: pnpm build (then pick a target such as pnpm dist:mac or pnpm dist:win)
notable: Plugin API with main, renderer, and preload hooks, plus config and menu support
Custom CSS themes loaded from the in-app Visual Tweaks options
Installable via Homebrew, Scoop, Winget, AUR, and Solus eopkg
Offline Windows install path using a nsis.7z file alongside the setup exe
Devcontainer support for building without installing dependencies on the host
caveats: Unofficial and not affiliated with Google or YouTube; provided AS IS with the user bearing all risk
Windows SmartScreen may block the installer as from an unknown publisher
GUI does not work in devcontainers on at least some Linux hosts
The README's themes section is missing its list of predefined themes
